Short answer: No. When working overseas you must use a company‑managed device and the approved VPN; personal laptops must not be used to access company systems. Access may also be restricted by country, network, data type, role, or system, and you must not access from a restricted destination [HR-POL-005 §4.5 Overseas access controls; HR-POL-005 §8. Decision Rules].

Also, international remote work requires prior written approval from your manager and People & Culture, including an Information Security and location‑risk review, before travel is booked [HR-POL-004 §5.3 International approval].

If you’re planning a trip, I recommend:
- Confirm your international remote‑work approval.
- Verify your destination isn’t restricted and that you can use the approved VPN.
- Arrange a company‑managed laptop if you don’t already have one.

If you share your destination and dates, I can point you to the specific requirements that apply.

  - Access requires a company‑managed device and the approved VPN. If the destination is restricted, access must not occur. If a device is lost or a security incident is suspected, report within one hour of discovery where personal safety permits; if evidence is incomplete, stop the risky activity and contact Information Security rather than improvising a workaround [HR-POL-005 §8].

If you’d like, share the destination country and dates and I can outline the exception request steps and checks required for a six‑week stay.

I’m sorry this happened. Here’s what to do according to company policy:

- Report it immediately. A lost or stolen company device is a security incident and must be reported within one hour of discovery, where safe to do so. Contact Information Security or the IT Service Desk and provide the last known location, time, network status, and any relevant account activity. Preserve messages/screenshots and don’t try to investigate on your own [HR-POL-005 §5.4; HR-POL-005 §5.3; HR-POL-009 §5.2]. If you’re not sure how serious it is—report it anyway; Security will assess [HR-POL-005 §10.4].  
- Don’t buy your own replacement. Expenses policy also directs you to use the equipment process for standard company items rather than personal purchase, and pre-approval is required for any exceptional reimbursement [HR-POL-006 §8; HR-POL-006 §4.4].  
- Don’t switch to a personal or public computer for company work unless Information Security grants a documented exception. Company systems must be accessed from a company‑managed device, and personal or public devices must not be used for access [HR-POL-005 §4.2; HR-POL-005 §9.2; HR-POL-005 §4.5].

If you’d like, I can help you draft a note to the IT/Information Security team with the key details to speed things up.

One quick question to help the report: when and where did you last have the laptop?

Short answer: No. Lawful personal travel does not, by itself, permit you to work from that country or access company systems there.

Key requirements and limits:
- Prior approval: International remote work requires written approval from your manager and People & Culture before you book travel, with Information Security and location‑risk review. Approval isn’t effective until all reviews are documented [HR-POL-004 §5.3 International approval].
- Restricted destinations: You must not work from or access company systems in restricted destinations. The company may decline a location due to confidentiality, connectivity, sanctions, tax, immigration, employment-location, insurance, or safety concerns [HR-POL-004 §4.5 Location restrictions; HR-POL-012 §4.2 Restricted destinations].
- Access controls abroad: If working overseas is approved, you must use a company‑managed device and the approved VPN. InfoSec may restrict access by country, network, data type, role, or system. Personal devices, public/shared business-center, and internet‑café computers must not be used. No access is allowed from restricted destinations [HR-POL-005 §4.5 Overseas access controls; HR-POL-005 §8. Decision Rules].

If you’re considering travel, don’t book yet. Share the destination and dates with your manager and People & Culture so they can run the required reviews and confirm whether access is permitted for that country and your role.
